paragraphs.text: DSH Web GUI sidebar glance card: DeepSeek balance, peak / off-peak billing countdown (statutory holi
days included), and today's spend / tokens / calls, right above the account row. Self-contained host
half; @linxin666/dsh-usage optional.
# dsh-account-glance
English | 中文
The live card: probed balance, Beijing peak / off-peak clock, and today's ledger.

A three-line glance card for the DSH Web GUI, seated **directly above** the sidebar's bottom-left
**
account / Settings** row:
| Line | Content |
| 1 | DeepSeek **account balance** — probed from `/user/balance` with the host-held API key; hover n

ames the source |
| 2 | **Peak / off-peak** billing period, with a live countdown to the next flip a

nd the discount in effect |
| 3 | **Today's spend / tokens / calls**, plus a **manual refresh** butt
on that forces one fresh probe |

Peak / off-peak follows DeepSeek's official schedule (Beijing time, UTC+8 all year): **peak** is
Mon
day–Friday `09:00–12:00` and `14:00–18:00` at full price, **every other hour** (nights and weekends)
plus **every Chinese statutory public holiday in full** is billed at **50% off**. The countdown swi

tches
to seconds for the final minute.
## Install
Needs **DSH 0.2.0-rc.1 or newer**. No other plugin, no dependencies, no build step.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The Plugins page also accepts the repository URL in its **Add plugin** dialog. Installing by hand: p

ut
the source at `<profile>\plugins\dsh-account-glance\`, add the package to both `dependencies` and

`dsh.profile.bundles`, then link it into `node_modules` (or run `pnpm install`). Do **not** add
`ac
count-glance` to `cordis.patch.yml` yourself — the package ships that row.
**Upgrading from 1.4.x:** the clock and price book changed (statutory holidays, v4-pro pricing), so
restart DSH (or toggle this row off and on in the Plugins page) and refresh the page once. From 1.3.

x it
is the same step — 1.4.0 introduced the host half.
## Turning it on and off
Sidebar **Plugins** icon → **Installed** → **dsh-account-glance**: the card switch toggles the whole
bundle, the row switch toggles this card. Instant — no restart, no refresh — and turning it off bri

ngs
dsh-usage's own glance card back.
## Where the numbers come from

Both data sources live in this plugin's own host half and are served over loopback-only routes
(`api
/dsh-account-glance/overview`, `.../refresh`); the API key never reaches the browser.

- **Balance** — `GET https://api.deepseek.com/user/balance`, with the key resolved from the DSH
cred

ential store (pi-ai record → configured env reference → ambient env). No probe value falls back to
t

he `account` Remote (Settings → Account & balance). A route pointed at a reseller is reported as
uns

upported rather than probed with the official endpoint; a failure keeps the last good number and
fla

gs the row.
- **Today's usage** — folded from the session event stream into a small per-day ledger a

t
`<DSH_HOME>/account-glance/ledger.json` (atomic write, 180-day retention), keyed by **Beijing date

**.
- **Cost** is priced for DeepSeek official routes only, from the published CNY peak / off-peak t

able
(flash and v4-pro each on their own row). Other routes — a DashScope-compatible provider, for
e

xample — still count tokens and calls, at cost 0, so a mixed ledger never sums two currencies.
- **H

olidays** — the official schedule bills Chinese public holidays as whole off-peak days. The table
sh
ips 2026 from the official notice and 2027 derived; a later year needs no release, only a file in th

official notice and 2027 derived; a later year needs no release, only a file in the
data directory:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Written to `<DSH_HOME>/account-glance/holidays.json` it is merged into the built-in table at startup
(`{ "replace": true, "holidays": [...] }` swaps the built-in table out instead — a replace file mus

t
then list every date you still need, including years the package already ships). The host applies

it
and serves the effective calendar to the card, so the badge and the ledger's cost column always a

gree.
- `@linxin666/dsh-usage` is **optional**: install it and nothing breaks — this card still read

s its own
route first, its glance card stays hidden, and its settings and usage pages keep working.
Probing is a read-only account query: no prompt, no tokens, no credit.
## Verify
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Both suites run offline. The client suite boots the shipped `lib/client.js` against React / DOM
stan

d-ins: seat and cadence, the probe outranking the account wallet, the fallback identity, the peak
cl
ock's eight boundary cases (statutory holidays included), the 15-second deadline, the refresh button

,
the degradation paths, and the dsh-usage fallback. The host suite covers the clock and price book

— the
shipped holiday calendar, the 2027 derived dates, and the per-profile override in merge, repla

ce and
malformed form — plus the ledger, credential resolution and probe shapes, the origin guard, s

ession
folding, the route fence, persistence across a restart, and the entry point.
## Known limitations
- Hiding dsh-usage's glance card relies on its `data-dsh-plugin="usage"` / `data-dsh-part="foot-card

"`
attributes; if it renames them, both cards appear (nothing breaks).
- The balance belongs to the

DeepSeek account the configured key belongs to — swap the key, swap the number.
- Cost appears for D

eepSeek official routes only; other routes show tokens and calls without an amount.
- With dsh-usage

installed too, both plugins keep their own ledger (this one buckets days by Beijing date,
dsh-usage

by host-local date), so the two totals can differ slightly.
- The built-in holiday table quotes 202

6 (国办发明电〔2025〕7号) and **derives** 2027 — the statutory dates
come from the lunar calendar, the bridg

e days follow the 2025/2026 pattern — so 2027 can shift when the
official notice lands. Correct it i

n the package, or per profile through `holidays.json` (see above).
- The card hides while the sideba
r is collapsed to its 56 px rail, matching the shell's own foot area.
